localChanges: The Enhanced rules in the game setup have four more boxes, each ticked, as the game already plays (#954).
A city you capture still stops building what it was, and you choose again; untick it to keep building it from no shields at your own price, as in the original (#954).
Every civilization's cities can still cause pollution; untick it to have only yours pollute, as in the original (#954).

Barbarian cities still build any attacking land unit that at least two civilizations can build; untick it to have them build only Swordmen, then Knights once anyone has Explosives, as in the original (#954).
Any civilization's cities can still set off a Barbarian uprising; untick it to have only yours set one off, as in the original (#954).

log: As v474.05's `uprising()`: `civ1-barbarians:turn/start/land-uprising` (`LAND_UPRISING_RULE`) rises only when the city drawn is a human's, and draws nothing more otherwise.

As v474.05's `find_slot()`: `civ1-barbarians:city/build/raiders-only` (`RAIDERS_ONLY_RULE`) allows a barbarian city one unit: a Warrior while the barbarians have no units, else a Swordman, else a Knight once any civilization has discovered Explosives.
Today's play for both (civ-clone/web-renderer#27) moves to `civ1-enhanced`, whose rule sets supersede these rules. On its own this changes play: release it together with `civ1-enhanced`.
civ-clone/web-renderer#954

As v474.05's `capunit()`: the shields are reset and Auto is cleared for every captor; a human captor keeps the item (`civ1-city:city/captured/keep-build`, exported as `KEEP_BUILD_RULE`), repriced and with the old owner's queue cleared; a computer captor chooses again (`clear-build`, now for computer captors only).

Today's play, the build cleared for a human captor too (civ-clone/web-renderer#670), moves to `civ1-enhanced`, whose rule set supersedes `keep-build` and clears through `lib/capturedBuild`. On its own this changes play: release it together with `civ1-enhanced`.
Every seat not played by the computer counts as v474.05's one human.
civ-clone/web-renderer#954

As v474.05's `city_process()`, where the pollution roll is inside `if (selected_owner == civnow)`: `civ1-city-improvement:city/process-yield/pollution` (exported as `POLLUTION_RULE`) rolls only for a human's cities. With no human seat it never fires.

Today's play, a roll in every city (civ-clone/web-renderer#32), moves to `civ1-enhanced`, whose rule set supersedes this rule and rolls through `lib/pollute`. On its own this changes play: release it together with `civ1-enhanced`.
civ-clone/web-renderer#954
Four more rule sets a new game can switch, each on to start with, as play was:

`civ1-enhanced:captured-city-build`: a city a human captures has its build cleared too, and its new owner chooses. Supersedes `civ1-city`'s `keep-build`. It runs before the city's capture is announced, wherever this package loads.
`civ1-enhanced:pollution-in-every-city`: every city rolls for pollution, not only a human's. Supersedes `civ1-city-improvement`'s pollution rule.
`civ1-enhanced:barbarian-city-builds`: a barbarian city builds any attacking land unit two civilizations can build. Supersedes `civ1-barbarians`' `raiders-only`.
`civ1-enhanced:barbarian-uprisings`: an uprising can break out near any civilization's city. Supersedes `civ1-barbarians`' `land-uprising`.
With every package loaded and nothing switched, play is as it was before these rules moved here.
civ-clone/web-renderer#954

The package depends on `@civ-clone/civ1-world-civilizations` and imports it, so a game with `civ1-enhanced` has the twelve civilizations the original does not: Sioux, Inca, Brazilian, Malian, Kongo, Ethiopian, Viking, Khmer, Indonesian, Japanese, Australian and Chukchi, with their leaders, traits, national themes and Earth start tiles. The original's fourteen are `civ1-civilization`'s.
civ-clone/web-renderer#954
